# Day 8: LPF or HPF in 30 seconds

- Date: Wednesday, August 12, 2026
- Block: Passives & filters
- Index: https://hardware.ellietaghavi.com/llm/index.md

## Equipment needed

*   10 kΩ resistor
*   10 nF capacitor
*   Breadboard and jumper wires
*   Oscilloscope
*   Function generator or MCU PWM

## Prerequisites

*   Understanding that a capacitor acts as an open circuit to DC and a short circuit to high-frequency AC.

## Introduction & background

Passive RC filters are the fundamental building blocks of signal conditioning. They rely on the frequency-dependent impedance of a capacitor. A powerful shortcut for analyzing any simple filter without complex math is to evaluate it at the extremes: assume the capacitor is a complete open circuit at DC (0 Hz) and a dead short at infinite frequency. By tracing where the signal goes under these two conditions, you can instantly categorize an unknown network as a low-pass filter (LPF) or high-pass filter (HPF).

## Core equations

$$f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi RC}$$

$$dB = 20\log_{10}\left(\frac{V_{out}}{V_{in}}\right)$$

## Diagram

[RC Low-Pass and High-Pass Filter Schematics](https://www.electronics-tutorials.ws/filter/filter_2.html)

## What you're building

1. A theoretical evaluation framework on paper to identify filters using the open/short trick.
2. A physical RC low-pass filter circuit on a breadboard.
3. A physical RC high-pass filter circuit on a breadboard.
4. An AC frequency sweep setup to find the exact −3 dB cutoff point for both circuits.

## Activity

On paper: for both RC orderings (series R then shunt C; series C then shunt R), replace the cap with an open circuit (DC) then a short (high f) and declare LPF or HPF. Then breadboard both with 10 kΩ/10 nF ($f_c \approx 1.6 \text{ kHz}$); sweep 100 Hz–100 kHz with the function gen or MCU PWM; find each −3 dB point.

## Question to answer

1. Does your measured corner frequency exactly match the theoretical $\frac{1}{2\pi RC}$?
2. What does −3 dB actually mean in terms of both power delivery and voltage amplitude?
